info.title: API.SH: Box Office Mojo
info.description: The Box Office Mojo API from API.SH: public Box Office Mojo data as clean JSON. Every endpoint is a GET with query parameters and your key in the x-api-key header. Calls that run cost the credits shown (x-credits): successes, and lookups that found nothing (404). Refused calls and errors on our side are free. Docs: https://api.sh/docs · Every platform: https://api.sh/openapi.json

get.summary: A brand's releases and grosses
get.description:
Every release of a brand (e.g. Marvel Comics, Pixar): rank, release, lifetime gross, max theaters, opening, release date, distributor. Each row carries every column the site shows, named after its header (money and counts as numbers), with linked ids (release, title, release group, distributor company, date or weekend) next to the column they come from.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/boxofficemojo-brand

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Brand id (`bn3732077058`, from `/boxofficemojo/v1/brands`) or a link.

parameters.name: area
parameters.description: Market code (`DE`, `GB`, `JP`, `FR`, `CN` ...; see `/boxofficemojo/v1/markets`); domestic (US and Canada) by default.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

parameters.name: area

get.summary: Domestic release schedule
get.description:
Upcoming (or a given month's) domestic releases: release date, title, release and IMDb title ids, poster, genres, cast, running time, distributor and scale (wide, limited, expands). `view=by_distributor` groups the schedule by distributor.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/boxofficemojo-calendar

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.summary: Daily box office chart for one day
get.description:
One day's domestic chart: today's and yesterday's rank, release, daily gross, change vs yesterday and last week, theaters, average, gross to date, days in release, distributor, new and estimated flags. Each row carries every column the site shows, named after its header (money and counts as numbers), with linked ids (release, title, release group, distributor company, date or weekend) next to the column they come from. Without a date, the latest day. `week=true` returns the full week from that day.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/boxofficemojo-daily

parameters.name: days_ago
parameters.description: The day this many days before today (instead of date).

parameters.name: week
parameters.description: The full week starting that day.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

example.name: Domestic Box Office For Saturday Nov 1, 2025

get.summary: Every day of a year (or of a month, quarter, season or holiday) with its #1 release
get.description:
Daily totals for a year: date, day number, top 10 gross and changes, number of releases, #1 release and its gross. `view` and `interval` narrow it to a month (`interval=july`), quarter (`q3`), season (`summer`) or holiday; `cumulative` shows the running year total. Each row carries every column the site shows, named after its header (money and counts as numbers), with linked ids (release, title, release group, distributor company, date or weekend) next to the column they come from.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/boxofficemojo-days

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

Each row carries every column the site shows, named after its header (money and counts as numbers), with linked ids (release, title, release group, distributor company, date or weekend) next to the column they come from.

get.summary: One release: daily, weekend or weekly grosses and rankings

One release in one market: summary (distributor, opening and theaters, budget, release dates, MPA rating, running time, genres, widest release), grosses, the other markets of the same release, and its day-by-day grosses (rank, gross, changes, theaters, average, to date). `view=weekend` or `weekly` gives the weekend or weekly run; `rankings` the charts it ranks on.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/boxofficemojo-release

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Release id (`rl2691925505`, from charts and titles) or a boxofficemojo.com release link.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.summary: A movie's box office: summary, releases by market, credits, rankings, similar
get.description:
A title's box office page by IMDb id: title, year, description, poster, summary (distributor, opening, budget, earliest release, MPA rating, running time, genres), domestic/international/worldwide grosses, every release group and the lifetime gross and rank per market. `view=credits` lists filmmakers and cast; `rankings` the charts it ranks on; `similar` similar titles.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/boxofficemojo-title

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: IMDb title id (`tt1375666`) or a boxofficemojo.com title link.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.summary: All-time charts: domestic, worldwide, inflation-adjusted, opening weekends
get.description:
All-time charts, 200 rows a page: top domestic lifetime grosses, worldwide lifetime grosses (with domestic and foreign shares), inflation-adjusted domestic grosses, and biggest opening weekends (domestic, international or one market). Each row carries every column the site shows, named after its header (money and counts as numbers), with linked ids (release, title, release group, distributor company, date or weekend) next to the column they come from. Pass `next_offset` back as `offset`; null on the last page.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/boxofficemojo-top

parameters.name: area
parameters.description: With chart=top_opening_weekend: a market code (see `/boxofficemojo/v1/markets`) or `XNDOM` for all international; domestic by default.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.summary: Weekend box office chart (any market, any weekend)
get.description:
A weekend chart: rank, last week's rank, release, weekend gross, change, theaters, theater change, per-theater average, total gross, weeks in release, distributor, new and estimated flags. Each row carries every column the site shows, named after its header (money and counts as numbers), with linked ids (release, title, release group, distributor company, date or weekend) next to the column they come from. Without year and week, the latest weekend; `date` picks the weekend holding that day. `view=by_distributor` totals the weekend per distributor.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/boxofficemojo-weekend

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: Any day of the weekend, YYYY-MM-DD (instead of year and week).

parameters.name: area
parameters.description: Market code (`DE`, `GB`, `JP`, `FR`, `CN` ...; see `/boxofficemojo/v1/markets`); domestic (US and Canada) by default.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.summary: Every weekend of a year with its #1 release
get.description:
All weekends of a year in a market: dates, top 10 gross and change, overall gross and change, number of releases, the #1 release, week number, long weekend flag. Each row carries every column the site shows, named after its header (money and counts as numbers), with linked ids (release, title, release group, distributor company, date or weekend) next to the column they come from.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/boxofficemojo-weekends

parameters.name: area
parameters.description: Market code (`DE`, `GB`, `JP`, `FR`, `CN` ...; see `/boxofficemojo/v1/markets`); domestic (US and Canada) by default.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.summary: Weekly (7-day) box office chart
get.description:
A domestic week's chart: rank, last week's rank, release, weekly gross, change, theaters, average, total gross, weeks, distributor. Each row carries every column the site shows, named after its header (money and counts as numbers), with linked ids (release, title, release group, distributor company, date or weekend) next to the column they come from. Without year and week, the latest week.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/boxofficemojo-weekly

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: Any day of the week, YYYY-MM-DD (instead of year and week).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.summary: Yearly box office chart: domestic, any market or worldwide
get.description:
The top releases of a year: rank, release, gross, theaters, total gross, release date, distributor. `area=world` gives the worldwide chart (worldwide, domestic and international grosses with shares). `grosses=total` counts each release's whole run instead of in-year grosses. Each row carries every column the site shows, named after its header (money and counts as numbers), with linked ids (release, title, release group, distributor company, date or weekend) next to the column they come from.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/boxofficemojo-year

parameters.name: area
parameters.description: Market code (see `/boxofficemojo/v1/markets`), or `world` for the worldwide chart; domestic by default.

parameters.name: grosses
parameters.description: `calendar` (default: grosses earned in the year) or `total` (releases of the year, whole run).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

apiKey.name: x-api-key
apiKey.description: Create keys at https://app.api.sh/keys. Authorization: Bearer <key> also works.

raw.name: raw
raw.description: 0 leaves out the bulky `raw` source blocks (often 10-30x smaller).

fields.name: fields
fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return, e.g. `posts.id,posts.title`. Call metadata is always included.

fresh.name: fresh
fresh.description: 1 skips the 24-hour cache and fetches live.

output.name: output
output.description: csv or ndjson returns the response's records (its main list, or the object as one row) as CSV or NDJSON instead of JSON.

records.name: records
records.description: With output=csv|ndjson: the top-level list to turn into rows (e.g. `reviews`), or `.` for the whole object as one row.

status_url.description: On a 503 for a paused endpoint: the status page, which lists open incidents.

E400.description: A parameter is missing or invalid. Not charged (unless the call ran and the source rejected the value; credits_used says).

E401.description: Missing, invalid, revoked or expired API key. Not charged. See https://api.sh/docs/errors#401

E402.description: Not enough credits, a spend limit you set was reached (`spend_limit`), or the key's monthly credit cap was reached (`key_cap`). Not charged.

E404.description: Not found, or not public. A lookup that ran costs the endpoint's price (credits_used says); an unknown route is free.

E502.description: The source site failed this time; retry. Not charged.

E503.description: Endpoint paused or temporarily unavailable; may include retry-after, and status_url (https://api.sh/status) for a paused endpoint. Not charged.
